findings.description: Issuer-pubkey trust gap at ucan_blobs_protocol::validate_request ARM 5. The wave-3e handler validates AuthorizationGrant.binding_sig using the issuer_verifying_key bytes EMBEDDED IN THE GRANT ITSELF (authorization_grant.rs:670 `VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&vk_bytes)` where `vk_bytes` is `self.issuer_verifying_key`). The handler does NOT chain that issuer-pubkey to a trusted root or known issuer-DID anywhere in the 6-arm pipeline. An attacker who controls any keypair can self-mint a grant with arbitrary (ucan, key_material, audience, scope) bytes, sign with their own key, embed their pubkey in `issuer_verifying_key`, and verify_binding will return Ok(()). The doc-comment at ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:273-275 ('the production wire-up accepts grants issued by other principals through the chain validator at the cap-policy hook') acknowledges the gap but no specific destination row is named in V1-FROZEN-INTERFACE-DEFERRED.md for this READ-side issuer-trust seam. (Distinct from §4.23's WRITE-side user-DID root-chain validator + distinct from Row D-26's PQ-hybrid wire-in.) At wave-3e fixtures the handler-keypair IS the grant issuer so tests stay self-consistent and never exercise the cross-issuer adversarial case.

findings.description: SAME-ATTACK-CLASS SIBLING GAP per feedback_d17_same_file_sweep_recurrence — AuthorizationGrant.audience_pubkey field has IDENTICAL attack-shape to the .scope field (which L3-r1-1 just closed by folding into binding_message) but was NOT swept in the L3-r1-1 fix-pass. CROSS-LENS CROSS-CONFIRMED with sibling L3 R6 R2 MAJOR (per orchestrator follow-up brief 2026-05-24 PM). Attack chain: (1) attacker obtains a legit grant bound to audience-CID-X (signed by issuer); (2) mutates `audience_pubkey` field to a different pubkey via constructor-pattern wedge (Option<Vec<u8>> field is freely mutable post-deserialize); (3) presents the tampered grant to handler. At ARM 2 of ucan_blobs_protocol::validate_request the connection EndpointId is byte-compared against the grant's MUTATED `audience_pubkey` (ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:442-460); if attacker SETS audience_pubkey to attacker's own EndpointId, ARM 2 passes against attacker's connection. ARM 5 verify_binding re-constructs binding_message WITHOUT audience_pubkey (only ucan / key_material / audience-as-Cid / scope are in the 5-segment layout); binding-sig still verifies. ARM 5 also checks audience_binding Cid matches the supplied audience but DOES NOT verify `audience_binding == Cid::from_blake3_digest(audience_pubkey)`. The audience_pubkey can therefore be repointed at runtime, redirecting the connection-EndpointId-bound trust path independently of the binding-sig. Production-arm impact: the wave-3e handler's stream-serve dispatch happens after ARM 6 if all arms pass, so a successful tamper redirects iroh-blobs serving to an unintended audience.
findings.evidence: crates/benten-caps/src/authorization_grant.rs:267 (`pub audience_pubkey: Option<Vec<u8>>` — post-deserialize-mutable); 390-425 (binding_message segments: domain || ucan-cbor || km-cbor || audience-cid || scope-len-u32-le || scope-cbor — `audience_pubkey` NOT in this list); 685-695 (verify_binding re-constructs binding_message WITHOUT audience_pubkey); crates/benten-sync/src/ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:442-460 (ARM 2 consumes grant.audience_pubkey for connection-EndpointId byte-compare); crates/benten-sync/src/ucan_blobs_protocol.rs:496-499 (ARM 5 audience check uses audience_binding Cid not audience_pubkey). findings.description: verify_binding does NOT include `issuer_verifying_key` in the binding_message. The current binding-message construction = `domain || ucan || km || audience || scope`. The issuer_verifying_key is parsed from the grant struct itself at verify-time + used to verify the binding-sig. Combined with MAJ-1 (no upstream issuer-trust check), this means: any attacker holding any signing keypair can self-mint a verifiably-valid grant for any (ucan, km, audience, scope) by signing with their own key + putting their own pubkey in issuer_verifying_key. Even if MAJ-1 is closed (chain check added), folding issuer_verifying_key into binding_message is the proper layered defense pattern (mirrors X-Wing combiner pubkey-binding pattern + the NF-4 commitment binding both pubkeys at sig.rs:467-477). Same-file sweep discipline (d17) — when extending binding_message for audience_pubkey (MAJ-2), also sweep issuer_verifying_key.

findings.recommendation: BELONGS-NAMED-NOW destination = SAME fix-pass as MAJ-2 — extend binding_message to bind issuer_verifying_key (commit to `Blake3(issuer_verifying_key)` if length-bound matters; otherwise length-prefixed-bytes mirroring scope shape). findings.description: Hybrid signature commitment comparison at sig.rs:473 uses Vec<u8> PartialEq which is non-constant-time. For a SHA3-256 commitment over PUBLIC inputs (pubkeys + sigs + msg are all public-known at verify time), timing leakage doesn't compromise secret material — the security property is preimage resistance of SHA3-256, not commitment-equality secrecy. The subtle::ConstantTimeEq pattern is the textbook recommendation for any crypto-equality comparison; subtle is already a workspace dep (crypto-suite Cargo.toml). Discipline-note rather than fix-now.
findings.evidence: crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/sig.rs:471-477 (commitment_expected != sig.commitment); subtle crate at crypto-suite Cargo.toml (already workspace dep). Reproducer: `grep -n 'subtle' crates/benten-crypto-suite/Cargo.toml` shows the dep is present; `grep -n 'commitment_expected' crates/benten-crypto-suite/src/sig.rs` shows the non-constant-time compare.
findings.recommendation: OBSERVATION ONLY — no fix-now required since the comparison inputs are public. If future R6 rounds surface ANY cryptographic-equality comparison whose inputs include secret material, codify a pim-N for 'subtle::ConstantTimeEq for crypto-equality compare' across the workspace + sweep this site to that standard then for consistency. Discipline-note can be carried at the bottom of authorization_grant.rs / sig.rs doc-blocks naming the public-input rationale.
